speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms better, have you noticed any changes in the color of your urine or stool, or any yellowing of your skin or eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I need to determine if the pruritus is associated with visible jaundice; have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or darkening of your urine? Additionally, have you experienced any recent fever, weight loss, or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and the presence of scleral icterus with pruritus, I suspect Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is unavailable, I will request an ultrasound of the abdomen to look for bile duct dilation and other structural abnormalities. I also need to check your blood work for specific autoimmune markers. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound, Anti-Mitochondrial_Antibody

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation. Anti-Mitochondrial Antibody: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening and dilatation, combined with your history of ulcerative colitis and negative Anti-Mitochondrial Antibody, strongly point toward Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. To confirm the diagnosis and assess for associated inflammation, I will order further specific liver autoantibodies and a liver biopsy. REQUEST TEST: p-ANCA, Liver_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal p-ANCA result is not uncommon in Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, so I will proceed with the liver biopsy results to confirm the diagnosis. Please provide the histopathology report from the liver biopsy. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal liver biopsy results contradict the diagnosis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, so I must reconsider the differential for a young male with ulcerative colitis, pruritus, and jaundice. Could you tell me if you have a history of recurrent abdominal pain, fever, or episodes of clay-colored stools that resolve spontaneously?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of inconsistent condom use and sexually active lifestyle, I need to rule out viral hepatitis as a cause of your liver dysfunction. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_Panel, Hepatitis_C_Antibody

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hepatitis B Panel: Negative, Hepatitis C Antibody: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral hepatitis and PSC ruled out, I need to consider metabolic causes of cholestasis such as Dubin-Johnson or Rotor syndrome, or perhaps drug-induced liver injury. Have you started any new medications, supplements, or herbal remedies recently, and do you have a family history of jaundice or liver disease?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, diarrhea, joint pain, or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of ulcerative colitis, cholestatic liver enzymes, bile duct abnormalities on ultrasound, and negative viral/autoimmune markers strongly supports Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, as p-ANCA and biopsy can be normal in many cases. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
